# SHWF-001 synthetic intake — demo-v1

This is fictional demonstration content. It is not actual bank material, regulatory guidance or evidence of approval.

Fictional Bank Alpha is exploring a read-only account-aggregation proposition. A fictional third-party app would display linked account summaries. Stage A uses no real customer records, identifiers, balances, credentials, bank APIs or consent grants.

The demonstration asks whether a reviewer can see the scope, responsible roles, missing evidence and outstanding decisions from one case workspace. It does not seek launch permission.

Illustrative bank role: LFI / data sharing. The actual role, applicability, inherited controls, bank approval procedure and evidence requirements must be established with the real case owners later.

Initial open questions: what is in scope; who owns the operations work; what template may be shared; who has actual decision authority; and what technical/provider/source boundary is acceptable?

# Illustrative workflow checklist — demo-v1

This checklist supplies synthetic discussion items, not regulatory obligations or a bank-approved control path. No statutory citations or compliance conclusions are asserted.

| Demo item | Discussion evidence to obtain later |
|---|---|
| Case scope | Confirm service, role, data/actions and exclusions with the case owner. |
| Consent journey | Identify the relevant consent journey and its owner; validate applicability separately. |
| Data boundary | Confirm permitted input/output data, retention and sharing rules. |
| Access | Confirm the application's actual user and file access model. |
| Operations | Name an operations owner and the support/exception process. |
| Document set | Identify which real templates may be used and shared. |
| Authority | Name the real decision makers and independent review rules. |
| Platform fit | Confirm services, licensing, region, providers and preview acceptance. |

A linked file is not proof that these items are satisfied. A typed owner name is not an authenticated decision. The demo operator must keep unmet items visible.

# S03 — provisional one-case charter extract

Synthetic design source, frozen 25 October 2026. This is a fictional one-case design charter, not a bank policy or accepted scope.

Use one fictional Bank Alpha LFI/data-provider account-data-sharing readiness case and one Readiness and Gaps Pack. A fictional third-party app would show account summaries. Use synthetic/public lab inputs only. Do not connect to bank endpoints, process customer records, initiate payments, create consent grants or execute a launch.

The first technical slice is structured drafting, automatically saved/registered pack, inspection and append-only comments. Case-specific controls and authorized approvals remain later work. A comment is not approval; an available source is not accepted evidence.

the bank sponsor's journey/role, one-pack content/format, named owners, permitted sources, platform hard stops, governing process, value criterion and participation answers remain pending. A change to TPP/data-recipient replaces this proposed case rather than adding another.


Origin: public synthetic fixture authored for offline contract and source-integrity tests.

# S04 — proposed architecture extract

Synthetic design source, frozen 25 October 2026. This summary of the public design sketch describes an implementation proposal, not a running or bank-approved system.

Codex assists development; Microsoft hosts the intended deployed runtime. Native Cowork Business apps/Work IQ preview submits Create-only proposals to Dataverse. Synchronous guards validate actual caller access, current revision, request identity and allowed fields. A PackDraft commits a proposal, business event and render job; an InspectionComment commits a proposal and event, with no render job or approval effect.

The renderer must automatically create a protected actual file and register its exact version/hash. Dataverse row access does not automatically protect SharePoint files. Native confirmation is not bank approval. Protected approvals and readiness gates require separate server validation and accepted authority policy.

Target-tenant tests, source boundaries, ordinary-user isolation, billing, renderer policy compatibility and bank admission are NOT RUN or NOT PROVEN. A local source file, typed actor or successful mock does not close them. Preview/provider/geography/private-network requirements remain bank-owner decisions.

Origin: the public design sketch, revised 25 October 2026. This fixture's wording is a declared summary; it is not a verbatim export or runtime provenance proof.
